samples.summary: New public `TextEditor.pasteFormat()` mutates the document with no internal `this.readOnly` guard, breaking the invariant the read-only design relies on
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3822-3828` states the read-only contract: "TextEditor's per-handler guards already block pointer / keyboard / clipboard events", and the `EditorAPI` allowlist is only the *second* layer. Every other mutating TextEditor entry point carries its own guard (`text-editor.ts:677`, `730`, `932`, `1439`, `1450`, `1888`). The lifted `pasteFormat()` (`text-editor.ts:399-407`) calls `saveSnapshot()` + `applyStyleToSelection()` with no `if (this.readOnly) return;`. `TextEditor` is a public export (`packages/docs/src/index.ts:111`), so the only thing preventing a read-only write through it is that `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2906` happens to be the sole caller and is neutered at `editor.ts:3850`. No live bypass exists today (the `Mod+Alt+V` key path is still gated by `text-editor.ts:932`), hence minor rather than major — the fix belongs on the new method.

samples.summary: The "one undo step" contract the new `setPageSetup` advertises is only exercised against `MemDocStore`; the production `YorkieDocStore` write path records no history presence and its `snapshot()` is a no-op
samples.evidence: `writePageSetup` (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:2006-2014`) calls `docStore.snapshot()` and nothing else, while the sibling direct-write path documents the requirement explicitly: "This direct toolbar/⌘B style path bypasses the text-editor's saveSnapshot hook, so it must set history state itself — otherwise the style op records no reversible presence and undo collapses the selection" (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1060-1075`, which calls `docStore.setCursorForHistory`). In the real app the store is `YorkieDocStore`, whose `snapshot()` is a documented no-op (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2793-2795`) and whose `setPageSetup` (`:2710-2720`) writes `root.pageSetup` inside a `doc.update` without `recordHistoryPresence`, unlike its sibling writes (`:2696-2704`). Pre-existing for the ruler's margin drag, but the new dialog widens it to paper size / orientation; `packages/docs/test/view/editor-page-setup.test.ts:141` proves undo only for `MemDocStore`.

samples.summary: `FormatPainterToggle` calls two brand-new `EditorAPI` members unguarded, and the frontend has no `tsc`, so any editor-shaped object missing them throws during toolbar render instead of failing to compile
samples.evidence: `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:102-103` calls `editor.hasCopiedFormat()` and `editor.onCopiedFormatChange(...)` directly (no optional call), unlike the file's other editor reads which use `editor?.x()`. Existing `EditorAPI` stubs in the repo do not supply them — `packages/frontend/tests/components/text-formatting/color-reset.test.ts:138-152` and `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/docs-formatting-toolbar-header-footer.test.tsx:39-52` — and survive only because the header/footer context returns early at `docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:539`, before the toggle is rendered. Every body-context caller (`docs-detail.tsx:215`, `shared-document.tsx:305`, `harness/hunt/page.tsx:772`) passes a real editor, so nothing is broken today, but the new hard requirement is uncheckable in this package.

samples.summary: Branch task doc ends with stray tool-call markup and cites test paths that do not exist in the tree
samples.evidence: `docs/tasks/active/20260829-docs-surface-existing-features-todo.md` ends with literal `</content>` / `</invoke>` lines (79-80) — leaked tool-call scaffolding, not document content. Its Review section (`:76-78`) also names `docs-format-painter.test.tsx` and `packages/docs/test/format-painter-api.test.ts`, while the files this change actually adds are `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/docs-format-painter-toggle.test.tsx` and `packages/docs/test/view/editor-format-painter.test.ts`; line 14 cites `text-editor.ts:997,1137` for symbols now at `:167` and `:3306`. Nested/active task docs are not covered by the backticked-path lane (only top-level `docs/design/*.md`), so nothing else catches this. No instruction-injection content was found in the files I opened.
